result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say plainly that the current numbers are not enough, and both give the director honest wording. A wins narrowly because it adds a delayed scenario re-check a week or two after the course and a check on whether the quiz tests decisions or recall; B never suggests re-checking what agents know later on. B lists concrete metrics with clear timing and names the small-sample and confounding problems more sharply, but its suggested wording for the director overclaims that agents are 'absorbing the content', and A's heavy use of bracketed placeholders makes it a little less concrete. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say plainly that completion, satisfaction and a same-week quiz don't show better job performance, and both give the director usable wording. A is stronger on honesty about causation, since it says outright that without a comparison group you can't separate the program from hire quality, team or seasonal volume. It also lists concrete metrics with 30/60/90-day checkpoints. B does better on a delayed knowledge re-check with realistic scenarios, but its bracketed placeholder metrics are less concrete and its causation caveat is weaker.
